questions.question: A client taking digoxin has a potassium level of 3.1 mEq/L. Which finding should the nurse report first?
questions.rationale: Low potassium raises the risk of digoxin toxicity. Nausea and visual changes like yellow or green halos are classic signs and need to be reported right away.
questions.caption: Digoxin + low K? Know your toxicity signs. Comment your answer before the reveal!

questions.question: Which lab value is most important to monitor for a client starting warfarin therapy?
questions.rationale: Warfarin is monitored with PT/INR. A typical target INR is 2 to 3 for most indications. aPTT is used to monitor heparin.
questions.caption: Warfarin vs heparin labs trip up so many students. Which one did you pick?
